title: Synthetic probes and adaptive alert tuning for request latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a coordinated system of lightweight synthetic probes combined with trace hooks and adaptive alert thresholds to reduce noisy paging and detect latent regressions that only show up in tail latency. This work spans: (1) probe design and placement across regions and instance types, (2) tracing instrumentation for synthetic requests so probes correlate to real traces, (3) metrics/log pipeline tagging to separate synthetic vs real traffic and feed anomaly detectors, and (4) alert tuning logic that adapts thresholds based on traffic seasonality and probe baselines.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic probes running in all production regions at low cost (<$0.30/day/region), emitting traces and metrics with tag synthetic=true
Traces from probes are hookable in the tracing system and linkable to existing request-span schemas (trace_id preserved, same span naming conventions)
Metrics pipeline emits a stable synthetic_latency.<region> metric and a synthetic_request_count metric; both are visible in the latency dashboard and queryable in the alerts engine

Alerting rules use probe baselines to adjust burn-rate thresholds and suppress pages for short-lived blips (configurable hysteresis). Paging noise reduced by 40% in staging compared to current thresholds
Runbook/playbook updated with probe incident triage steps and a toggle to mute synthetic-driven alerts
End-to-end smoke test and canary: two-week canary showing no increase in undetected user-impact incidents and improved early detection of regression introduced in canary model
notes: Design decision: probes will be lightweight (single request, typical prompt, ~512 tokens max) to limit cost while still exercising KV cache hot paths and batching behaviors
Trade-off: More frequent probes increase fidelity for tail latency but also add noise and cost. We picked a 1m cadence for critical regions and 5m for low-traffic regions as an initial compromise
We will tag probe traces with attribute 'redwood.synthetic=true' and add a provenance field 'probe_id' to track probe variants
Alerting strategy: use probe percentiles to compute a dynamic baseline and apply multiplicative factor + minimum absolute floor before firing burn-rate alerts
Retention: probe traces will be sampled at 100% for 48 hours then downsampled to conserve storage
We decided against embedding probes into real user requests (shadowing) due to privacy and cost concerns; probes are synthetic but follow common request patterns
implementation_steps: Add SDK helper for probes (probe client) to generate instrumented requests and trace context
Deploy probe runner as a k8s CronJob + replicated daemonset in each region with rate-limited concurrency
Update runtime trace hooks to accept 'redwood.synthetic' tag and forward to tracing backend
Modify metrics/loki pipeline to add 'source:probe' labels and create dedicated metrics series
Implement adaptive threshold module in alerts engine that reads probe baselines and computes dynamic burn-rate thresholds
Canary rollout: enable adaptive alerts in staging for 3 regions, evaluate noise reduction and missed-detection rate for 14 days
Full rollout and monitoring + revert plan if synthetic alerts increase false negatives
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: probes skew platform load and affect real traffic. Mitigation: strict rate limiting, run probes on isolated capacity pools when possible
Risk: synthetic traces cause alerting parity drift vs real traffic. Mitigation: keep a small set of 'shadowed' real-request baselines for cross-checking
Risk: storage costs for full probe traces. Mitigation: 48h full retention then aggressive downsampling
Risk: onboarding complexity for on-prem Private deployments. Mitigation: provide an opt-in probe runner and clear docs for Private customers
